Thick white frost rims every dead console and creeps up the walls, the air so cold it hangs visible and still.
Drifting debris and tiny frozen droplets hang motionless in the zero-g dark, slowly turning where the explorer's movement disturbed them.
Scattered personal effects drift slowly — a single boot, a cracked photo-frame, a mug — the small human traces of a vanished crew.
A long scorch-streak and a jagged hull breach scar one wall, the metal peeled outward, frost feathering the torn edges.
Every screen is dead and dark, but one flickers weakly in a long cycle — static, black, static — and then nothing again.
A thin grey dust layer coats every flat surface, undisturbed for years, softening the edges of consoles and fallen tools alike.
Ice sheets the corridor walls in smooth pale slabs, locking a smear of old grease and a handprint into permanent cold glass.
Tangled cables drift free of an open panel, swaying in the faintest air current like slow dark weeds below still water.
Rust-bloom spreads across the bulkhead in wide orange halos, eating outward from every rivet, the metal soft and flaking at the edges.
A snapped strut hangs diagonally across the passage, its fractured end crystalline and jagged, frost filling every split like white mortar.
Emergency foam, triggered in some final crisis, froze mid-spray across a doorway — pale and rigid, still shaped like the moment it burst.
Claw-scored panels line one section of wall, long parallel gouges dragged deep through the plating, the metal curled at each groove's edge.
A body-shaped void sits in the command chair — frost everywhere except that outline, the cold recording an absence where someone last sat.
Impact cracks web outward from a single point on the viewport, each fracture line traced white with ice, the glass still holding barely.
Corrosion has furred every exposed copper contact into pale green velvet, the terminal strips soft and crumbling at the faintest touch.
A drifting photograph turns very slowly near the ceiling — two people, smiling, the image bleached almost white by years of cold exposure.
One ceiling panel has buckled downward and hangs at an angle, frost-heavy and cracked, a dark gap yawning above it into dead conduits.
Loose bolts and a small wrench float in a loose constellation at eye level, abandoned mid-repair, orbiting nothing in the cold silence.
A coffee mug drifts in a long slow arc through the compartment, a frozen brown disc still inside it, the handle pointing nowhere.
Frost feathers every vent grille in delicate white crystal formations, growing inward and outward both, the airflow that shaped them long dead.
A pressurised locker stands open, its contents spilled in a frozen scatter across the floor — ration packs, a torch, a folded silver blanket.
Oxidisation has turned one entire access panel a deep liver-brown, the surface blistered and rough, bolts so corroded they have fused permanently shut.
A single warning light still pulses somewhere deep in the walls — slow, amber, nearly dead — casting a faint heartbeat of colour and shadow.
Hairline fractures run the full length of one load-bearing column, packed with ice that has slowly forced the cracks wider over cold years.
The galley wall holds a roster written in marker — names, duties, dates — the ink faded nearly invisible beneath a pale rime of frost.
